case_study_insert.main_stem: Quay Street Marketplace (QSM) is a private limited company in the online retail and e-commerce sector, employing a workforce of 26. Founded in 2016 by Nadia Quay, the platform sells its own craft giftware range through a website and mobile app alongside independent sellers and runs a flat structure with laissez-faire leadership. QSM plans to invest $520,000 in an automated stock-control and dispatch system, financed by a $320,000 five-year bank loan and $200,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $150,000 a year, a variable cost of $9 a unit and a selling price of $17, and currently produces 55,000 units a year. QSM faces two problems: staff turnover is rising and dispatch errors have increased.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Market Research and Operations Summary, Q3 2025: QSM processed 13,200 orders last quarter with a dispatch error rate of 1.9%, down from 3.6% last year. Complaints about late delivery fell from 47 to 22 per month. Average order dispatch time is 2.8 days. A survey of 380 marketplace buyers found 71% value fast delivery most, and 46% would pay up to $0.90 more for carbon-neutral shipping. Records show 9 of 26 staff have not completed on-the-job training on the new stock-control system; off-the-job training courses at the local college cost $680 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Financial Position of Quay Street Marketplace as at 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank raised the base interest rate from 4.25% to 5.25%, increasing borrowing costs for businesses with variable-rate loans. (2) The national minimum wage rises by 6.1% from $13.10 to $13.90 an hour from April 2026. (3) Packaging and shipping input costs have risen 8.7% year on year, while online marketplace spending grew 5.4%.

questions.question_text: QSM plans to fund part of its automation with a five-year bank loan. Explain two advantages for QSM of using retained profit to finance the expansion instead of the bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Retained profit carries no interest or repayment schedule, so QSM protects the cash needed to run a marketplace with fixed costs of $150,000 a year and a $320,000 bank loan already outstanding. Cash saved can absorb the 8.7% rise in packaging and shipping costs without raising the $17 selling price for the 71% of surveyed buyers who value fast delivery.

Point 2: Using $200,000 retained profit avoids the collateral and covenants of a bank loan, so the $520,000 stock-control and dispatch system is not endangered if sales fall short. It also preserves Nadia Quay's control of the platform instead of handing influence to lenders, letting QSM respond quickly to the 46% of buyers who would pay $0.90 more for carbon-neutral shipping. Faster decisions suit a small 26-employee e-commerce firm.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage of retained profit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to QSM's costs, finance and survey evidence.

questions.question_text: QSM is promoting its carbon-neutral shipping option. Consider a national television campaign, search-engine advertising, or social media influencer marketing. Which should QSM choose to promote this option? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Television campaign: A national TV advert would give QSM's marketplace instant mass recognition and could attract new sellers and buyers. However, airtime is expensive for a 26-employee business investing $520,000 in automation, and most viewers do not shop on niche craft platforms, so the spend would be largely wasted.

Search-engine advertising: Paid search targets buyers searching for craft giftware or carbon-neutral delivery, is measurable and can be strictly budgeted, which protects cash flow alongside the $320,000 loan. Its weakness is that it only captures people already looking, so it cannot create demand for a new shipping option among the 46% of 380 buyers who would pay $0.90 more but may not yet know QSM offers it.

Social media influencer marketing: Craft and lifestyle influencers can show the carbon-neutral option to an engaged audience that already buys online, matching the 71% of buyers who value fast delivery and building trust in the platform. It is cost-effective and measurable, though results depend on the influencer's credibility and can take time to accumulate.

Recommendation: QSM should choose social media influencer marketing with a small search budget. It reaches the right online community, explains the $0.90 carbon-neutral proposition and costs far less than television, which is rejected as unaffordable and untargeted. Search alone is rejected because it cannot generate the awareness needed for a new option.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited description of promotional methods with minimal reference to QSM.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discussion of advantages and disadvantages of at least two methods applied to QSM's online marketplace.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three methods with a justified recommendation that rejects television and explains the limits of search advertising.

questions.question_text: QSM's staff turnover is rising and dispatch errors have increased. Explain two benefits for QSM of using laissez-faire leadership to improve motivation in its operations team.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Laissez-faire leadership gives the 26 staff freedom to decide how they organise dispatch, which suits a flat structure and can raise job satisfaction and reduce the rising staff turnover. Skilled workers who choose their own routines are more likely to stay, cutting the cost of repeated recruitment and helping protect the 13,200 orders processed each quarter.

Point 2: Allowing staff to solve problems themselves can reduce the 1.9% dispatch error rate, because those closest to the stock-control system see faults first and can act without waiting for approval. Autonomy also makes the $680 college training more valuable, as employees apply it directly, supporting the $520,000 automation and the 2.8-day dispatch time.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit of laissez-faire leadership identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to QSM's turnover, errors, structure and training.

questions.question_text: QSM must train 9 staff on the new stock-control system. Consider on-the-job training or off-the-job training at the local college. Which should QSM choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Learning at the dispatch desk is tailored to QSM's own system, costs no fees, and keeps the 9 staff handling the 13,200 orders processed each quarter. It directly targets the 1.9% dispatch error rate and fits a flat structure where experienced colleagues coach others. Drawbacks are that the coach's work slows, mistakes can be copied, and no formal certificate is awarded.

Off-the-job training: College courses at $680 per employee cost $6,120 for the 9 staff, a small fraction of the $520,000 investment. They provide structured, up-to-date skills and a recognised qualification, useful as the platform grows. However, staff are away from the dispatch desk, worsening the 2.8-day dispatch time, and generic content may not match QSM's system, so on-site follow-up would still be needed.

Decision: QSM should choose on-the-job training, with short college updates later. It is cheaper, specific to the stock-control system and avoids losing output while staff turnover is a problem and dispatch errors remain. Full off-the-job training is rejected because $6,120 and the absence of 9 staff would slow the 2.8-day dispatch promise during automation, and laissez-faire leadership works best with coaching on the job.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to QSM.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analysis of benefits and drawbacks of both methods in QSM's context with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both methods with a justified decision covering cost, disruption, error reduction and system relevance.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how QSM's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $150,000 ÷ ($17 − $9) = $150,000 ÷ $8 = 18,750 units. Answer: break-even output is 18,750 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $17 − $9 = $8.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $8.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways QSM's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare break-even output of 18,750 units with output of 55,000 units to show a margin of safety of 36,250 units, confirming the new dispatch system can be used without losses.
2. Use the $0.90 premium that 46% of buyers accept to model contribution rising from $8.00 to $8.90, helping set the carbon-neutral shipping price.
3. Plan volumes that cover $150,000 fixed costs and $320,000 loan repayments, checking the 55,000-unit plan can service debt.
4. Track unit cost ($150,000 ÷ 55,000 + $9 = $11.73) each quarter to benchmark automation and detect waste behind the 1.9% dispatch error rate.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 18,750 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $8.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety against 55,000-unit output; modelling the $0.90 carbon-neutral premium; loan-service volume targets; and unit-cost benchmarking at $11.73 to monitor dispatch errors.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method and 1 mark for the accurate numerical answer in each of (i) and (ii); 1 mark per valid applied use in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate QSM's financial position by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has QSM's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.69 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 1.85 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 1.25 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 1.32 : 1

Detailed workings: 2024 current assets = $46,000 + $72,000 + $58,000 = $176,000; 2025 current assets = $58,000 + $61,000 + $84,000 = $203,000. For 2024, $176,000 ÷ $104,000 = 1.69; for 2025, $203,000 ÷ $110,000 = 1.85. Excluding stock: 2024 ($176,000 − $46,000) ÷ $104,000 = $130,000 ÷ $104,000 = 1.25; 2025 ($203,000 − $58,000) ÷ $110,000 = $145,000 ÷ $110,000 = 1.32.

Evaluation: Liquidity has strengthened. Coverage of short-term obligations rose from 1.69 to 1.85 as current assets grew by $27,000 while liabilities rose only $6,000. The stock-excluding measure also improved, from 1.25 to 1.32, so QSM is better placed to meet debts without relying on inventory — valuable while it services a $320,000 loan and spends $520,000 on automation. Cash rose from $58,000 to $84,000 and receivables fell from $72,000 to $61,000, freeing cash. Inventories rose from $46,000 to $58,000, which should be watched given the 1.9% dispatch error rate, but the overall liquidity trend is favourable.

Conclusion: QSM's financial position has improved. Both measures rose and the stock-excluding measure confirms the gain is not caused by higher inventory alone. Falling receivables and higher cash reinforce the improvement, so the automation can be funded with confidence.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates both ratios for both years with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations with detailed evaluation of inventory, receivables, cash and liabilities and a justified conclusion.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for QSM of introducing carbon-neutral shipping for its online orders.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Carbon-neutral shipping appeals to the 46% of 380 surveyed buyers who would pay up to $0.90 more, protecting the $8.00 contribution per unit as packaging and shipping costs rise 8.7%. It also supports the $520,000 automation by differentiating the marketplace from rivals.

Disadvantage: Low-carbon packaging and courier options usually cost more, raising the $9 variable cost per unit unless the full $0.90 premium is accepted by all buyers. Any slower delivery would conflict with the 71% who value fast delivery most and could lengthen the 2.8-day dispatch time, risking the 1.9% dispatch error target.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to QSM's survey data, costs and expansion.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 5.25%, the 6.1% minimum wage increase and the 8.7% rise in packaging and shipping costs will affect QSM. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.25% to 5.25%): If QSM's $320,000 five-year bank loan is variable-rate, the annual interest cost rises by 1.0% of $320,000 = $3,200 a year (0.01 × $320,000). This is small against fixed costs of $150,000, and if the loan is fixed-rate the direct cost is zero. Higher rates could slow online spending and raise future borrowing costs for the $520,000 system, but the exposure is limited.

Minimum wage increase (6.1%, to $13.90 an hour): With a workforce of 26, higher hourly pay lifts QSM's wage bill and cannot be avoided. The insert gives no hours worked or individual pay, so an annual figure cannot be invented; the defensible test is productivity of 55,000 ÷ 26 = 2,115.4 units per worker. If productivity holds the rise is manageable; if it falls, the $8.00 contribution per unit is squeezed.

Packaging and shipping inflation (8.7%): The $9 variable cost per unit is exposed, but the insert does not break it down, so only an illustrative bound is honest: if the whole variable cost rose 8.7%, that adds 8.7% × $9 = $0.78 per unit, roughly $43,000 a year at 55,000 units. The $0.90 premium accepted by 46% of buyers can offset much of this.

Conclusion: The 8.7% rise in packaging and shipping costs has the greatest impact. It recurs on every unit, directly threatens the $8.00 contribution supporting the $520,000 investment, and is only partly offset by pricing; the interest rise is small and the wage effect depends on hours not stated in the insert.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external changes with limited application to QSM.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two changes on QSM's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three changes in QSM's context with a justified greatest-impact judgement that avoids invented figures.
